relevance_note: Cohort plus literature review of Alexander disease; Table 1 ties seven novel GFAP mutations to CNMC patients, one of them individually described: "A unique mutation (R66Q) was detected in one deceased patient".
method_note: Patient-level data are in online table e-1 (CNMC patients) and table e-3, neither of which is in the converted text; the rest of the paper is group-level statistics over 215 patients (30 new CNMC cases, 185 previously published). The only individual-level content is Table 1 (novel GFAP mutations in the CNMC cohort; one row per mutation, no patient label column) and its footnote. I made one individual row per Table 1 data row, labelled 'Table 1 row k' (k = 1..7 from the top, below the header row 'Base pair change | Amino acid change | Exon | Protein domain'). The paper does not say how many patients carry each novel mutation, so each row stands for at least one carrier; if a mutation occurred in more than one CNMC patient, the extra carriers are not represented. Table 1 row 1 (c.211 G>A, R66Q) is the deceased patient of the footnote, with no parental testing; inheritance left not reported. Rows 2-7 take inheritance 'de novo' and pathogenicity from the footnote's named-group statement 'In all other patients parental testing determined that the mutation was pathogenic and de novo.' Protein changes are printed as one-letter codes without 'p.' and recorded as printed; the cDNA strings contain a space ('c.211 G>A'), kept as printed. Exon and domain columns were not recorded (no schema field). No phenotype is given for any individual except the brain-biopsy finding for row 1; all checklist items are not reported. Spans and rows were built with a short script reading the paper's Table 1 lines, checked against the table. No contradictions found.
